legend: It is almost Valentine's Day and Bob has found the perfect gift for Alice: a permutation of the integers 0,...,n−1%%ZSMJ0%%! Bob knows that MEX is Alice's favorite function, and for this reason he wants to write for each index i%%ZSMJ1%%, the sum of MEX over all subarrays of the permutation that contain index i%%ZSMJ2%%. Unfortunately this is difficult for Bob to compute so he needs your help.

Formally, you are given a permutation a1,...,an%%ZSMJ3%% consisting of (distinct) integers 0,...,n−1%%ZSMJ4%%. For each 1≤i≤n%%ZSMJ5%%, determine the sum of MEX(a[l,r])%%ZSMJ6%% for each 1≤l≤r≤n%%ZSMJ7%% where a[l,r]%%ZSMJ8%% represents the subarray al,al+1,...ar%%ZSMJ9%%, and MEX(b)%%ZSMJ10%% outputs the smallest non-negative integer k%%ZSMJ11%% such that k%%ZSMJ12%% doesn't appear in b%%ZSMJ13%%.
input: The first line of input will contain a single integer n%%ZSMJ14%% (1≤n≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ15%%) — denoting the size of the permutation Bob found. The next line will contain n%%ZSMJ16%% distinct integers a1,...,an%%ZSMJ17%% (0≤ai≤n−1%%ZSMJ18%%) — describing the permutation itself.
output: The output will consist of n%%ZSMJ19%% lines. On the i%%ZSMJ20%%th line, output the sum of MEX over all subarrays of a%%ZSMJ21%% containing index i%%ZSMJ22%%.
